When we hymn God, when we receive His praise, as far as possible, becoming in perfection, we sing a new song; for that which is in perfection is uninterrupted. Therefore also the hymn which is sent up to God thankfully within it is a new song.

Many shall see and shall be afraid and shall hope in the Lord (Ps 37:7). 'Many shall see,' having seen me lifted up from the pit of misery and from the mire of matter, and having my feet established upon the rock, and my steps being directed, and me singing and hymning; 'and they shall be afraid' so that they too might come into such a guidance, 'and they shall hope' so that they too might attain these things which already exist for me.

Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord (Ps 37:7). David once had a single combat against Goliath and did not hope in a shield. You see that the name of the Lord has become his hope. And it is said regarding the Lord being signified by hope—and there is no other hope than the expectation of good things—that often some say of things already existing, 'my hope.' The wealthy indeed say 'my hope,' not regarding what is expected, but what is already present. And therefore, those who already possess the name of the Lord consider it to be hope.

And he did not look toward vanities and false delusions. He who looks toward the Lord does not look toward vanities and false delusions. He does not look toward wealth, nor toward greatness of body, nor toward military might, nor toward any other of those things which are able to fail. And 'delusions' are called 'false,' the divinations. They are...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Distinction Between Human and Divine Thought
english: And indeed these manias are not false; for instance, those receiving God or those receiving Christ are god-bearers, and these manias are not false but true, instead of being 'repressed.' For if they were not also true manias, he would not have said: 'he who has had a false hope regarding madness' (1 Cor 6:9). Those according to the Phrygians, not having been ignorant of how these things are said, taking both the meaning of madness and of ecstasy, call the spirit-bearing men as having spoken in ecstasy or having prophesied. And they speak truly regarding ecstasy, but not regarding derangement or insanity.

If indeed Paul says: 'whether we have gone out of our minds, [it is] to God' (1 Cor 6:9), he is not speaking of madness, but of standing outside of human [limits] and... [gap]... having given. And this word is also said regarding wonder: 'And after these things the sons of Israel will turn back and will seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they will be astonished at the Lord and in His good things' (Ps 142:7). He signifies wonder here.

'You have done many things, Lord my God, Your wonders' (Ps 142:5). Having been tested by the doing of the things spoken, since he did not only enjoy these good things, but—so that I may say this—was drawn to these from childhood—and so indeed His anointing while being a child has happened paradoxically, and he says: 'You have done many things, Lord my God, Your wonders.' Many and great things are, 'and with Your thoughts' (Ps 142:4), according to which You do wonders, 'no one shall be like [You].' No one is able to do such wonders; no one is able to bring someone out of the pit of misery and from the mud of matter and set his feet upon a rock and direct his steps and the other things.

The 'there is no one who shall be like' if said in reference to the Father, does not speak concerning the Son; for none of the begotten shall be like [the Father]. But the Son is not [to be] compared; for He is eternal, the icon and character of the divine essence. There is not...

Having the future of becoming like [Him]; for he is like. Regarding: the 'thoughts'? Thoughts are primarily called the thoughts concerning each individual thing. Just as the act of reasoning is a conversation of the soul, and it is not possible to say many things at once, so also the thoughts concerning each individual thing are called thoughts.

A logical place is given for asking whether knowing is the same as reasoning, and it has been said that they are not the same; for there are many things known without reasoning, and many things reasoned about without being known, so that knowing is not the same as reasoning. One is able to grasp a concept of a whole genus and of a whole species. But to know each individual thing, each being reasoned about by itself, it is not possible to do all at once. Regarding: so that the reasoning is upon sensation? But it is upon the individual things being reasoned about. Just as it is not possible to say many things at once while knowing many things, since the intellect is a kind of speech of the soul, it is not possible to reason about many things at once.

God, therefore, has such thoughts that He knows all things at once, yet in a different way than men; for in Isaiah He said: 'As the heavens are far from the earth, so are your thoughts from my thought' (Isaiah 55:9). He wished to show the superiority of His own intellect through a sensory example; for His intellect has not stayed away from the intellect of men locally, but by a greatness of superiority. And with your thoughts no one shall be like. No one is like the thoughts of God. Just as you would say: 'No one shall be like the creation of God.'

For even if they were creators among men, they do not construct the underlying matter of the things coming into being. For example, if a craftsman makes a bed or a throne, he does not make the wood by his art. He only imposes the end upon the previously taken matter. But God, not finding matter, imposes the form upon it, but rather composes it with the form. I have declared and I have spoken, they were multiplied beyond...

title: The Spiritual Sacrifice and the Fulfillment of Scripture
english: Regarding number. You know that if we do not conceive something as necessary and do not desire to report it to another, how can we ever say 'thus and thus', when we know that we have not sat down to say what we intended? And this one therefore says: 'I have reported and I have spoken'. Since none of your thoughts is like 'I have reported and I have spoken'. It can also be taken this way: 'I have reported' according to the intention, according to the thought, and 'I have spoken' perceptibly according to the utterance; for first it is necessary to conceive, then thus to speak.

Regarding: 'They were increased beyond number'? —the thoughts, to which none is similar. You did not desire sacrifice and offering. Therefore he says: 'He brought me up out of the pit of misery and out of the mire of filth, having set my feet upon a rock, having directed my steps' (Ps 40:2). How much it was necessary to sacrifice and to offer as a burnt offering to God regarding these Christological words and the even greater benefits! But you did not desire the perceptible burnt offerings, the bodily sacrifices from the slaughter of animals and others, the shadowy ones. 'A body he has prepared for me' (Ps 40:6). Instead of these, the apostle has interpreted that this body is the logical and bloodless sacrifice. When therefore a greater sacrifice is found, then he no longer wants the former; they are no longer desired by him.

Let not the [words] of the Diimorites trouble you; for they say: 'Do you see that [it is] a body'? —for the one saying 'a body he has prepared for me', this he says as 'only'; for even one having a perfect man has a body, but not only. And I said the psalm was one-personed from the beginning; for from the beginning to the end the same speaking person has entered. Just as he said here: 'but a body he has prepared for me', and in the following he says: 'those seeking my soul, let them seek it'. Behold, he has a soul also, behold, he has a body also.

And since the word is concerning the perceptible sacrifices superseded by the Spirit, he spoke of the succeeding sacrifice. It is not the soul that becomes the sacrifice according to this meaning, but the body. And it is also good that [it is not] 'he prepared', but himself 'he has prepared', 'the Holy Spirit having come upon' Mary 'and the power of the Most High having overshadowed her' (Lk 1:35). Because of this, you no longer desired those sacrifices and offerings, since 'a body he has prepared for me' which is to be offered on behalf of all. And this can be said: because of this, [he] th...

You did not desire a physical sacrifice and offering, since I have prepared for us a body, which we are able to perform as a sacred rite and sacrifice to you; 'I urge you through mercies to present your bodies as a logical sacrifice' (Rom 12:1). In other [interpretations] it is said: 'And you have prepared ears for me.' One interpreter says this: since you did not desire a sensory sacrifice and offering, 'you have prepared ears for me,' through which I hear those things concerning the things made manifest by the sensory, such as the intellectual sacrifice of understanding: 'sacrifice to God a sacrifice of understanding.' Furthermore, if you call me to a lecture, you no longer seek sensory things being performed, so that what is said might be like: 'The Lord's instruction opens my ears' (Ps 119:16). An unmusical man does not have ears for hearing musical words.

And another of the interpreters said: 'You have dug out ears for me,' since you removed their dullness, you removed that which obstructs hearing. Furthermore: regarding Jesus, how do we receive him? —I said that the 196 allegories are not smoothed out to match the histories. And often I omitted the matter of Abraham and the two women. I said to you that the soul of Jesus is not an unshakeable essence. It is of the same kind as the others, and everything it has that is good, it has from the Word of God. Since therefore it also has the ability to hear well, it has that from the Savior. It surpasses the temple in which it is housed.

7 You did not seek burnt offerings and [things] concerning sin. Nor did you seek, nor did you still delight in the things of the shadow. 'What multitude of your sacrifices to me [is there]? I am full. I do not want the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of lambs' (Ps 50:6). 8 Then he said: 'Behold, I have come' (Isa 6:8). Then I, for whom a body was prepared, said: 'Behold, I have come,' instead of [saying]: since the purpose of his coming is this, to receive the end of the shadow, so that sacrifices and burnt offerings are no longer brought, I have come, in order to fulfill the sacrifice by becoming a burnt offering.

8 It has been written in a heading of a book concerning me. The heading of a book is called 'all inspired Scripture'; for the main point of the Scripture is the life [rule of life] concerning Christ. According to a second account, let it also be said concerning others; for if the coming were not about to happen, the old writings would not have prefigured the Gospel. Furthermore: was this written during the Pentateuch? —He says every Scripture is a book, whose heading is the end for which the writings are given, which is salvation, the coming. Furthermore: the Genesis...

title: Opposition of Wills and Spiritual Food
english: Therefore, was the world foretold for this reason? So that He might bring the generation of the world to its completion through humans, and after this generation of humans, so that the epidemic might take place. 'Lamb' is 'of God, who takes away the sin of the world' (John 1:29). Regarding the saying that Adam transgressed 'through disobedience' and the Savior 'through obedience' is justified (Rom 5:19), it is not making a comparison concerning the Savior, who is a type of the one to come, since Adam himself 'is a type of the one to come'; 'this great mystery is, and I say it refers to Christ and the Church' (Eph 5:32).

But since it is not entirely, if a book is said to be, it must be taken according to perception; Ezekiel hears from God: 'open your mouth' (Ezek 3:3), and he sees a book upon the hand of God, and says: 'take it and eat, and your belly shall be filled' (Ezek 3:3). 'And I ate', he says, 'and it became sweetness in my belly'. And he says: 'this book is written within and without' (Ezek 3:3). According to the spiritual and intelligible things it is written within, according to the sensible and manifest things without. But the wise man devours both and finds harmony between the symbols and the originals.

And in Isaiah he says again: 'and these words shall be as the words of the book of the sealed, if they give it to a man knowing letters, saying: take, read. He says: I cannot, for it is sealed' (Isa 29:11). And the illiterate man says: 'I do not know letters'. He was asking whether it differed if it were sealed or not sealed. And we take again the God-breathed Scripture, the one knowing letters but unable to read because of the placed seals being the circumcised people, and the one not knowing letters being from the Gentiles.

'To do, O God, your will I have desired' (Ps 40:8). Therefore 'I said: behold, I have come' (Heb 10:7), since the will was desired to do your will after you did not desire me for sacrifice and offering. Those who hold false doctrines concerning Christ say that there are different wills; for even here he says: 'I have come, I desire to do your will', in the Gospel: 'I have descended from heaven not to do human will, but the will of him who sent me' (John 6:38). Therefore, concerning those saying that there are two wills, we say that: the different wills occur either according to more or less or...

In opposition. The one progressing in virtue desires righteousness, and the one perfected [does too], and the will of the perfected is not the same as that of the one progressing or the one being led in. For there becomes either a multitude or a duality of wills according to the more and the less, and it also happens in opposition, when one chooses good things and another evil, and one wills to be saved and another to sin. Therefore, such a will as this, to approach the Son having opposition, is the extreme of impiety.

Furthermore, I also direct [this] toward the Manichaeans. One must act toward these: the will of the Savior is found to be good; for he says, having come down from heaven, 'that I might do the will of God' (John 6:38). And to do the will of God is good. And again: 'The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost' (Luke 19:10). And again: 'If you wish, you are able to cleanse me' (Mark 10:51). If this is the will of the Son, he wills all things that are beneficial. But since the will of the Father is being opposite to him, I leave it to you to consider. If it is found according to the more and the less in wills and in disposition, then both the Father and the Son will have a disposition, that is, a way of acting, and the Father is no longer without body, nor is the essence without connection. Nor is it to be said according to the more and the less, nor in opposition; for the will of the Son is demonstrated to be good. Yet it is not right according to God to say, however, that this is his will, to perfect the will of the Father. It is not right according to God to say [this]. Nor is it opposite, nor according to the more and the less. Therefore, one must take these things regarding the man.

And 'your law in the midst of my belly' (Psalm 119:11). It is spiritual food containing [itself] in the belly of the inner man. And the law, which is evident everywhere, is spiritual food; for it is not sensible food. This belly is often praised, and in the [psalm]: 'From the fear of you in the belly we have received' (Psalm 119:11). And just as this belly receives in the belly from the divine spirit—which is the fear of God—so also it receives divine food into itself. No longer desiring your sacrifice or offering or burnt offerings, having the spiritual law as food. I have evangelized righteousness in a great church. 'Great church' is the one of the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Union of Truth and Mercy
english: Consisting of great things, concerning which Paul says, 'we speak wisdom among the perfect' (1 Cor 2:6), so that the sum of these is a 'great church.' This is not the righteousness according to the law, about which the apostle says, 'having become blameless according to the righteousness in the law' (Rom 3:19). This then righteousness I preached to the great church; for if the letter and the shadow were not preached to the great [ones], but to infants.

But what kind of righteousness? —about which the Savior was saying, 'unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees' (Matt 5:20), is this not according to the shadow? Therefore yours—of the disciples—the Savior says, let the righteousness exceed theirs. And he says that theirs was with ignorance. Because of this, let us not be ignorant of the righteousness of God, but let us preach it.

10 Behold, my lips I will not restrain. 'Lips' here means the word. Often when he is called to say something to small and imperfect men, we restrain our lips; we do not have them released, but we descend with them, we speak cryptically, we speak proverbially, and our lips are restrained. But when to the perfect and a great church, since he does not restrain his lips, since he does not hinder them from speaking anything. And it is possible also to say this: as the [psalmist says]: 'and in his law he will meditate day and night' (Ps 1:2). He never restrains his lips, always bringing forth the words of God. And the 'always' hear it thus: as it is necessary and as it is fitting to do this; for even if he is silent, he speaks in his mind, and even while sleeping, when he sleeps as a righteous man, he does this with the word. And through silence, he remembers something good.

10–11 Lord, you have known my righteousness (Ps 26:3). Since much of what is said has testified to himself—for 'to preach righteousness in a great church' is great and, so that I may say this, beyond man—he says to God: 'you have known my righteousness' (Ps 26:3). This [righteousness], which I announce, I possess and have practiced according to it. And if the psalm were even speaking about the man of the Savior, that: since he did not know sin, but the sin that has come to be, it is productive of righteousness. And this is also possible: even if some, being ignorant, speak blasphemy against me, but you know my righteousness. As also Susanna said: 'you know that...'

What false things testify against me? I have not hidden your truth in my heart. He who has known the righteousness of God does not hide the truth joined to it in his heart. Truth is called joined to righteousness when it says: 'Truth has risen from the earth, and righteousness has stooped from heaven' (Ps 85:11). Regarding the Savior, he says righteousness is stooping from heaven; for he says: 'He bent the heaven and came down.' And 'risen from the earth' means having reached the end of the visitation. But it can also be understood thus: when from the earth, that good and beautiful soul has risen after having heard the word and having been fruitful. Therefore righteousness stoops from heaven. And in another psalm he says: 'Mercy and truth met, righteousness and peace kissed' (Ps 85:10). Those who read histories find that wars and disturbances arise from unrighteousness. But truth has the mercy of God; for if God does not show mercy, no one is able to know the truth, how much and what it is. Therefore 'mercy and truth met.' And mercy is also possible, such as he who loves his neighbor as himself is merciful to his neighbor and himself requires the same mercy from him; for indeed the truth is made manifest. Just as righteousness leads peace, so also the mercy of truth. Moreover, both are one and the same. If then Jesus and his words are ashamed, his truth is ashamed. 'And I have spoken my salvation' (Ps 116:16). The confession of the truth is my salvation. If he also says the truth concerning Christ, he again says Christ is the salvation, and 'I have spoken my salvation and revealed your truth.' I speak of the salvation being the Christ whom I make manifest. 'I have not hidden your mercy and your truth from a great assembly' (Ps 51:1). We say that mercy is joined to the truth. And 'a great assembly' means those from the Gentiles who have believed, having been gathered from all the Gentiles. And the wise man says this, and Jesus also according to the man. 'And you, Lord, do not distance your mercies from me' (Ps 51:1). I have come to your mercies, blamelessly and as is necessary. Do not therefore distance them, so that I may remain such. 'Let the [mercy] quickly overtake us...'
The text ends abruptly with a fragment of a quote.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Lawlessness of the Inner Man
english: “Your mercies, Lord, for we have become extremely poor” (Ps 51:1). If the mercies are lengthened, poverty occurs. He who is guarded from that from which the mercies did not lengthen is rich; and he is rich in having received the truth and mercy. “Your mercy and your truth have taken hold of me continually” (Ps 51:1). Your mercy and your truth have taken hold of me, the one in need. “Do not lengthen” therefore “your mercies” (Ps 51:1), so that your truth, being taken hold of, and the mercy joined with it, might remain thus.

“For evils surround me, of which there is no number” (Ps 51:8). For this reason, “do not lengthen your mercies from me” (Ps 51:1), because many evils surround me, not falling under number, that is, because of multitude—if the heavy things are signified, because of multitude they do not have a number. But if the other evils, the practical ones about which it is said, “a fool does evils in laughter” (Prov 26:11), they are not in any word or number; for they are not of things that exist, they are thoughts of men, transgressions of divine laws. Therefore, take the double meaning of the evils.

“My iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see” (Ps 51:13). And it is also possible to take it thus: “for evils surround me” (Ps 51:8) not falling under number—as has been said now, in two ways—for this reason: “for my iniquities have overtaken me” (Ps 51:13). But from another beginning it is to be read, joining the “for evils surround me” (Ps 51:8) to “but you, Lord, do not lengthen your mercies from me” (Ps 51:1), “for evils surround me, of which there is no number” (Ps 51:8). Let both then be considered: “your mercy and your truth have taken hold of me continually” (Ps 51:1). Here, therefore, he says this: he calls the habits iniquities, and the iniquities' powers are being brought under. “My iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see” (Ps 51:13); for they are harmful to the eyes of the mind, providing blindness to the inner eye of man. Since, therefore, they have overtaken me, I am not able to see. And these habits can also be taken...

The previous explanation dealt with the active powers. And they themselves, having seized me, pursued and seized me by the hand, and because of this I am not able to see; for the lawlessnesses of the inner man are harmful to the eyes. They were multiplied beyond the hairs of my head (Ps 51:11), and my heart has forsaken me (Ps 31:10). If you wish, these sins, they seize [one] when someone falls by them and sins; for having suffered this, the intellect of the soul is harmed. And if also the active powers of them, they are often called similarly by the name of passion.

“And my heart has forsaken me” (Ps 31:10). Since the lawlessnesses that seized me and removed my sight “were multiplied beyond the hairs of my head” (Ps 51:11), “my heart has forsaken me” (Ps 31:10), I no longer have the heart of a wise man; for the heart of the one saying these things is fleshy. When therefore the fleshy heart forsakes someone, it becomes stony.

“Be pleased, Lord, to save me” (Ps 51:11). Since the lawlessnesses seized [me] and I am not able to see and they were multiplied beyond the hairs of my head (Ps 51:11), “be pleased to save me” (Ps 51:11), so that the heart may not remain forsaken. If the word was about these hairs of this head, he has spoken hyperbolically; for if lawlessnesses occur, they are not able to exceed the number of the hairs of the head. Therefore it is spoken hyperbolically.

But if not, he says this: for the hairs of my head—that is, the unfeeling movements that are not truly fitting to the mind—are hairs; for the unfeeling things in us are also hairs that touch. This therefore he says: having seized my lawlessnesses and being no longer able to see, the hairs of my head were multiplied, the things unfeelingly thought, the things thoughtlessly intended. Because of this my heart, the mind itself, has forsaken me. It is no longer my mind, being dragged down into sin. Lord, to help me.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Poor Man's Cry and the Blessedness of Sharing
english: Pay attention. For I ask you to be pleased to rescue [me], not for the sake of another, but so that you might attend to helping me. And help me, if you make [me] outside of those ruling wars.

Those seeking my soul were greatly ashamed and were simultaneously ensnared. They were saying that the Psalm is about a single person. But if the one speaking is a man, he sends up a prayer concerning both, both for the body and for the soul. Therefore, if 'the Son of Man'—the Temple who has come forth from Mary—says these things, we shall say to those saying that only the body was taken: 'But He said, "He shall keep my body"'—see, even this He says, and it is the same person who is announcing it. Those who know the truth are turned back and are ashamed.

Those wishing evil upon me turned back toward the rear and were ensnared. It is a great thing to have turned the evil toward the rear; for to continue onward is harmful. Therefore, 'turning toward the rear' means 'they turned back' so as not to increase the road, not to rush forward. May those saying to me, 'Well done, well done,' be immediately clothed in shame. There is a wish regarding what he says, 'immediately,' that they may not remain in the evil, that they may not unceasingly say, 'Well done, well done, well done.' To say 'well done, well done' mockingly when something unpleasant is happening to those suffering is [wrong].

May all those seeking you, O Lord, rejoice and be glad. Having spoken concerning the adversaries, so that they also might be ashamed and be ensnared and turn toward the rear, saying mockingly 'well done, well done,' he says: 'May all those seeking you, O Lord, rejoice and be glad.' Then we rejoice and are glad when, having sought, we find you; for he who seeks something rejoices and is glad when he finds it. Even if, therefore, troublesome or other harmful things come upon [us], we seek to find you as a help. Then, appearing to be a help, you say: 'I will say while you are still speaking: Behold, I am here.'

And let them say at all times: Let the Lord be magnified. Since, having found you, they give thanks, saying, 'Let them say at all times: Let the Lord be magnified,' they might have those things for which they owe praise and rejoicing. It is possible to 'say at all times'; may ingratitude never exist for them. Those who love your salvation. The justice...
salvation, or the cause becoming salvation to them, or about to become salvation. 'Let the Lord be magnified always, let them say.' Loving your salvation, they magnify God always because of it.

18 But I am poor and needy; the Lord cares for me. Therefore I pray that your help may come to me and that you may be pleased to rescue me, because 'I am poor and needy.' I am not able to encourage myself, I am not able to do for myself from the outside regarding the things lying ahead, unless you help. 'Poor' therefore 'I am, and needy.' The difference between these two has been said at other times.

18 You are my helper and my protector; you are my God, do not delay. Since I have called you as a helper and a protector putting forth your shield for me—and this is the truth; for 'truth shall surround you as a weapon' (Ps 5:12)—'do not delay,' lest the struggle become too much for my strength. When you know it is the right time to care, to help, and to rescue, let this happen; for as far as my power and my nature reach, I am weak to help myself, to do for myself regarding the impending evils.

290 1–2 To the end; a psalm of David. Blessed is he who shows compassion to the poor and needy. And many take this psalm from the person of the Savior because of the way words lying here are received in the Gospel as having been spoken by the Savior and having been done and seen concerning the Savior. 'Blessed,' he says, 'is he who shows compassion to the poor and needy.' And many have explained such things regarding the character of the act, saying: the needy and the poor are different; and he who shares with these ought, according to analogy, to practice sharing; for he acts with understanding. It is not necessary to feed all those who are in want. Nor is it the case of one lacking food because he previously sought it thoughtlessly—he indulged in drinking, and everything he had he consumed unseemly and foolishly—but rather [one lacking] because of sickness or because of much childhood dependency. It is therefore necessary to provide to each with understanding. If anyone does not have enough to give to all, he ought to do this with understanding to those to whom he is obligated to give; and if he is able, he should also become a benefactor to others, according to the Father in the heavens, who causes the sun to rise not only upon the good but also upon the evil (Matt 5:45).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Body as a Bed of Suffering
english: However, since one cannot satisfy everyone, let him do this with understanding. This can be understood regarding the Savior: for he 'became poor through us' [2 Cor 8:9] and not for the sake of another. 'He became poor through us' so that he might free us from poverty and turn us away from want. He says, 'the one who did not know sin, for our sake made sin' [2 Cor 5:21]—this is his poverty—'so that we might become the righteousness of God in him.' [Fragmentary text] It was asked... it was not sustained. Even if sin occurred, it was not so that sin might remain, but so that he might free the... 'You know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that being rich he became poor for us' [2 Cor 8:9]. And the paradox is this: 'being rich' he is poor, and this poverty makes us rich, for it is a creative poverty. He is not poor at all, but in relation to his wealth.

2 In a day of evil the Lord will deliver him. He delivered Jesus 'in a day of evil' [Matt 27:22-23], when those surrounding him were saying, 'Crucify, crucify him; we have no king but Caesar.' And it was also asked from that evil day, how he, having become sin, became a creator of righteousness. The name of understanding is taken for the sake of doing good to brothers in need; for the apostle says regarding an offering: 'Understand what I say; for God will give you understanding in all things' [1 Cor 12:8]. And understanding is the knowledge of things joined together and things not joined together. Joined things are those that are similar, those that are equal, when we bring one thing to another and find that it has identity either by similarity or by equality. The one, therefore, having understanding, knows which things are joined to which and which are not.

3 The Lord will preserve him and let him live and make him blessed in the land. This can be said of both: the Lord preserves the poor and the needy. For this reason he also led the one understanding into himself. Where has it ever been said: when you see a suffering person and one who has arrived suddenly under another pretext, look there for a physician; see that the word of the divine providence has touched the physician, a compassionate physician, so that, sympathizing with the sufferer, he might help him medically. But he blesses the poor and needy man and makes him live in the land, or the one understanding and having received understanding upon...

The poor and the needy. If you speak concerning the Savior, you protect him and provide for him to live; for even though 'he was crucified in weakness, but lives by the power of God' (Heb 13:3). Take 'in the earth' in a common sense.

And do not hand him over into the hands of his enemies. Such a person does not hand over 'into the hands of his enemies.' Such a person has many enemies, many who are attacking him; for he is a blessed man and has understanding toward the poor and the needy according to all the clarifications provided, and he has many [enemies] attacking him; for God will rescue him from their hands. But he who is given over to them is not rescued from the hand of those persecuting him.

The Lord will help him upon his bed of pain. Here, concerning the poor, he says: even if he should be upon a bed of sickness and such a thing should be painful to him, God helps him. Have the things said in the Gospels concerning the paralytics: one remained in a bed of pain for thirty-eight years, thrown down on a bed so as not to be able to be shaken or to rise up (John 5:5). And others like these were recorded in the Gospels as paralytics. But not everyone upon a bed of pain and sickness is rescued. For instance, one fell from the bed from on high and died.

But if toward a restoration, the body is often called the bed of the soul. And there are many scriptures gathered together for such a theory. When someone is in the corruptible body and dwells in the earth, he 'reaps a much-wise mind' (Job 4:7), [he] is 'upon a bed of pain'; but when God helps him, he makes him to lift up the body and to carry it away, and he is no longer thrown down upon the body, but he himself afterwards lifts up the bed and walks. The body, therefore, is a bed.

The lover of pleasure, the lover of passion, the one accepting and doing the things of the body, suffers upon a bed, but God helps him and makes him healthy, so that, having become healthy, he may no longer be thrown down upon the bed himself, but he himself may carry it, and as they say, so that the soul may begin of the body. What then are those sixty powerful ones, who are received in blessing, who are around the bed? From Abraham to nineteen and from... these, therefore, are the sixty powerful ones concerning the body of...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Sin against God and the Enemies of the Savior
english: Having served the Savior by his birth. It must be said thus: the world came into being in six days, and sixty is a perfect number, as it has been often demonstrated; for in tens, sixty-six is [present]. Therefore, he who surpassed the world and having gone above is able, being a 'man trained for war' (Ps 45:3), having a sword 'upon his thigh' (Ps 45:3). Concerning the bed of Solomon, these sixty are able, concerning the Lord's body, circling it, observing, by what cause the Savior was incarnated. 'Sixty' therefore [are] 'able around it, all holding a sword'. They are swords. And the swords which the wise hold are swords. 'The righteous shall rejoice in glory and shall exult in their throat' (Ps 97:11), 'and a two-edged sword in their hands' (Ps 45:3). They have two-edged swords in their hands. And they also have [it] 'upon the thigh'.

And since the drama concerning the marriage of the bride and bridegroom is a bridal chamber, he says the temperate ones concerning the bridegroom, to show, and he says that they have a sword upon the thigh, cutting away shameful desires. 'You turned his whole bed in his sickness' (Job 33:25). This says: he did not give a brief healing to the one greatly sickened, but 'turned his whole bed' (Job 33:25) away from the sickness, so that he might no longer be sick, but might be healthy, as I said concerning the paralytic. And you also say concerning Lazarus, the one being drawn out having a body, that, when he was taken up from thence by the angels, his whole bed was turned, his whole sickness. He was no longer laid down in sickness. Instead, he was being carried into the bosom of Abraham.

'I said, Lord, have mercy on me' (Ps 51:3). Instead, he says that: what was upon us was achieved, to be rescued from the bed of sickness and to be helped from the bed of pain; for I did this, 'I said, Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you' (Ps 51:3). You see that, when he sinned, then he was in [trouble] and then he was laid upon a bed and a couch. When therefore anyone knows Him who is able to rescue, he will attain to the one who is striving, similarly to him: 'I want, be cleansed' (Mark 1:41), 'Rise, take up your bed and walk' (Mark 2:11). 'I' therefore 'said, Lord, have mercy' (Ps 51:3). By saying: 'Lord, have mercy on me', I showed that I was not able to be pitied by myself. I healed.

I have sinned against you, I have sinned against you. In this way, almost all of us sin toward God, knowing much about Him through ignorance and doing much contrary to His laws. 'I have sinned' is thus 'against you'; but having said, 'Lord, have mercy on me,' he possesses the petition.

My enemies said evil things to me: 'When will he die, and will his name be destroyed?' (Ps 54:1). I say that this psalm is to be spoken from the person of the Savior according to man. And since the Jews have become His enemies, like traitors to the truth, having not understood the one who came among them, and since Judas also became one of the disciples, regarding the enemies he speaks singularly of those having risen up against him—once in reference to Judas as the beginning of the betrayal, and once plurally because of those following him and having overthrown Jesus.

And it is not only here that this happens, but also in the 108th psalm it is said: 'They spoke against me with a deceitful tongue, and with words of hatred they surrounded me. Instead of loving me, they attacked me, but I was praying; and they set evil against me instead of good, and hatred instead of my love. Set the sinner upon him, and let the devil stand at his right hand' (Ps 108:2-5)—this he says singularly concerning Judas—'in the judging of him, let him go out condemned, and let another take his oversight' (Ps 108:8). Once therefore concerning Judas, and once concerning those who agreed with him, he speaks; and for this reason in the same verses where there is singular, there is plural.

And thus he says: 'My enemies said.' This they said: the evil things which they think are evil, they said against me: 'When will he die, and will his name be destroyed?' (Ps 54:1). For they thought that after the death of Jesus his teaching and his fame would be extinguished, and they said: 'When will he die?' On the contrary, it went the opposite of what they thought. His name did not shine forth less when he lived and was alive than when he was crucified and taken up. And for the correction of those of heterodox opinion, this is to be taken: for as many as do not think rightly, but are being deceived and say impious things concerning the Savior, they are the ones who spoke evil against him. And since there is a leader of the heresies, the false speaker, or even his slandering devil, through...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Lawlessness of Judas
english: He also speaks similarly regarding this matter. For, did the soul of the Savior sin? The soul of the Savior is the whole of the significant part, not when it sins. Just as we say 'God is man', so also 'the soul of Jesus'. At times we say the soul of Jesus, which is the one he received, and at other times the soul of Jesus, thus the one made his own, according to what is signified by the saying, 'All souls are mine'. And if all are the Savior's, then each one is too.

For, did the soul of the saints sin? It is said that the soul of the saints sins in this way: when it occurs in a pre-passion. And often we use that example: a garment that has been cleaned, if it receives some stain from touching something, it does not appear at all as stained. But if you take for me a completely clean garment, having just come from the dye-vat, even if you touch it, it is said to be stained.

For, does the body not become in sin? My soul becomes in a pre-passion; for it 'began' 'to be amazed and to be distressed'. From here, those who attribute the so-called irrationality to Jesus are refuted. An irrational animal is able to begin to be amazed, but not to be distressed; for to be distressed is foreign to an animal. From the being distressed and from the being amazed, they attached the beginning to him. But there is no beginning after the pre-passion; just as a passion is not a beginning, but the pre-passion itself is. And in another psalm it is said: 'My upholder; I shall not be shaken any further' (Psalm 62:7). For, what is being distressed? It is sorrow of the rational soul along with the inability to discern the causes of the sorrow.

Regarding the remnant of Judas, he says: if ever 'he went in to see, but in vain he ran' (Gen 45:22); just as we said recently, that he who possesses something more has more words concerning others than other men, so also Judas had something more than the other traitors; for he benefited from much time and had the legacy and the spark of his instruction. Therefore he entered many times toward Jesus, as also in the fellowship he was found.

It was not the Passover, but rather 'he was speaking falsely' when he said, 'Rabbi,' and loved him. He says, 'Whatever you do, do it quickly.' He was manifesting words of honor toward Jesus. But he was speaking falsely—for in order to show to those coming for his arrest, he had spoken these things, not so that he might truly manifest the reverence he previously showed toward the teacher. Therefore, all things that are not happening according to the truth are spoken falsely.

7 His heart gathered lawlessness unto himself. Even if his heart gathered lawlessness, it was to no one else but himself. 'What do you want me to do? And I will hand him over to you.' His heart gathered lawlessness in doing this when he gave his heart to the devil; 'and the devil entered after the morsel into him' (John 13:27). Therefore, Judas has committed lawlessness. To betray Jesus, the enemy of the teacher who had benefited him so much, was lawless. Thus, this lawlessness, which he gathered thinking that he was surrounding his teacher with death, he gathered for himself; for he did not touch him. He therefore rose from the dead, and all their efforts... greatness was shown.

7 He was going out and speaking. This happened... and after some honor he approached, whether 'he was going out'—his heart regarding... that they would come for the arrest of Jesus, saying, 'This is he, seize him' (Matt 26:48). 'He was going out... and he was going out.' Some indeed have become accustomed to say that there is neither outside nor inside. The end... because he betrayed Jesus. 'Knowing,' he says, 'that he was condemned, having gone away, he despaired.' 'Knowing that he was condemned'—Jesus by Pilate—he was greatly distressed, 'and having gone away, he despaired.' 'Having seen that he was condemned' himself, after the betrayal of such a distant teacher.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Winging of the Man of Peace
english: He was handed over, and having gone away, he approached with life as a burden. All my enemies were whispering against me; none of them spoke against me with boldness. And you find the Jews seeking how they might take him secretly; they were whispering to Judas, and he to them; for he did not enter a synagogue and shout this: 'What do you want to give me, and I will hand him over to you?' (Matt 26:14-15). Indeed, they themselves did not come to seize him for forty days.

This is what Jesus himself says: 'I teach every day' (Matt 26:21) in the synagogue, and now 'as if I had come to a robber.' They set a lawless word against me. They were reading the Scriptures 'every Sabbath' so that they might learn the things of the law. And from the opposite, it was necessary for those reading with the law to know who is the one prophesied and testified to by the Scriptures; they set a lawless word against me, saying: 'This one does not cast out demons except by Beelzebub.' 'If this man were from God, he would not have loosed the Sabbath' (John 11:45). 'Is it not bad that we say, "You are a Samaritan and have a demon"?' This is the one against whom they set a lawless word. And it is possible, since even in the legal briefs 'he set' is often taken; voices were set against Pilate concerning him.

Does he who is sleeping not add to rising? Rather, he himself says: since death surrounded me, I slept; for in the Scriptures the name of sleep sometimes signifies death. Sleep is also called slumber, and the union of a man with a woman is called sleep. And death is also called sleep according to the Scripture because of the expectation of the resurrection; for just as he who sleeps, if he suffers no harm to nature, might be raised, so the dying man will be raised. Thus indeed it is said, 'all shall sleep,' and, 'I do not want you to be ignorant concerning those who have slept' (Acts 1:3), that is, concerning mortals. For the Greeks say this.

And indeed the man of my peace, on whom I hoped. The 'I hoped' here is 'I took courage' concerning the man; for the Gospel also mentioned this, that this one 'the man of my peace lifted up a wing'; for they were saying that even in the fourth Psalm of Pentecost concerning him it says, 'But you, O man, my equal soul' (Ps 41:9). 'If my enemy...

He would have mocked me, or even if the one hating me had magnified himself against me, I would have been hidden from him. But you, my soul's equal—we take this regarding the one of one accord, and again 'the woman in your bosom' is your equal—'my leader and my savior'. They had as leader, not as ruler, but as my leader, running before me. And here: 'the man of my peace, in whom I hoped' (Ps 4:7).

It is nothing wonderful if you whispered against me and set a lawless word against me, if 'the man of my peace' has become the beginning of this evil of yours. Therefore he 'raised up' 'the wing', not the head 'against me'. The one eating my bread magnified a winging against me. 'The man of my peace, in whom I hoped' (Ps 4:7), 'he raised up his wing against me', he wished to wing me. It is a fluttering... and Jacob is called a winger; for he winged Esau when [he took] the blessing [of the] elder. To set upon someone with deceit is called a winging. It is someone... to lead [them] so that he might take his garment. And he who deceives toward the death of someone...

But you, Lord, have mercy on me and raise me up, and I will repay them. Make me outside of the evils and of the bad winging of the lawless word which they set against me. These things again are said more humanly concerning the man Jesus. 'But you, Lord, have mercy, and I will repay them.' I shall be their judge. The one who rises to repay and to judge, as he finds the dispositions, gives back. Many, having experienced harm or seeing that they once condemned [him], himself is about to judge them, according to: 'they shall look upon him whom they crucified' (Jn 19:37), they come into knowledge and they know how the due retribution persists toward them.

In this I knew that you willed me. This is knowledge and proof that it is your will to have me; for in this they shall know me. The 'in this I knew' does not refer so much to his own knowledge, but rather that those of mine shall be known in this. Above all, having been condemned, will they know him?—all having received a perception of his greatness, whether they were enemies before or acquaintances. Because my enemy shall by no means be pleased with me. When I am shown as your will, when I rise and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Meaning of Understanding
english: Let it be known that according to your will, both Judas and the devil who worked in him are able. To make them rejoice, he surrounded him with death; but upon his resurrection they do not rejoice, but rather they experience shame and stand in fear, having seen the one they had betrayed. But you took hold of me through my innocence. For I did not know sin, even though I have become sin; even though I have become a curse, I was not shown to be a curse because of a preceding sin, but so that I might loose the curse and provide a blessing. And just as it has become sin so that God might make righteous those for whom sin has become, so it has become a curse, not so that it might be held by the curse. This very thing, then, has become a curse upon a blessing, sin upon righteousness, death received for life.

Innocence, then, often signifies the absence of something, and it is when there is complete purity from sin. But when it says, 'the simple believes every word' (Ps 119:7), and also, 'bad associations corrupt good morals' (1 Cor 15:34), it speaks of the surrounding good morals. And complete virtue is also called innocence, concerning which he says, 'the simple and upright cling to me' (Ps 15:2). And you have established me before you for ever. Not for a little time, then, did I not slip, being simple before falling to enemies, but I remained simple; for 'you have established me' indeed 'for ever.' Not simply, then, but 'before you.' And not everyone who is being established is additionally established by God, but he who has the perfection established. 'He who establishes you with us in Christ.' So, you testifying to my innocence.

Blessed is the Lord God of Israel from ever and to ever (Ps 102:28). Let it be, let it be. The one having mind regarding Israel, seeing God, is a blessed God. To him I write the grace and the victory, not by our power; for even if I am simple, I do not give the whole by my innocence, but by the cooperation of God. The 'let it be, let it be' is like the 'amen' as other interpreters say. And the 'amen' is when it is taken instead of an oath; for when it says, 'truly I say to you,' Matthew and Luke write the same word, and Matthew says, 'Amen, amen, I say to you,' but Luke says, 'Truly I say to you.' Indeed, it is also said in the writings, 'Behold, the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to [your word]' (Lk 1:38).

"Your word." It is also said by those interpreting the Hebrew sounds that it means that which is believed. To the end; for understanding, to the sons of Korah, a psalm. Three sons of Korah became temple singers. And their names are brought forward in Exodus and in the Chronicles. These, just as some take from faith one soul and one heart, so also these, having received one soul from the uniting spirit which grants the singing, because of this they bring forth the verses of the psalm in unison.

And this psalm is not one filled by chance with mysteries. Because of this, "for understanding" is inscribed. Thus also in the thirty-first [Psalm] we say that it is "of the understanding to David," because he contained mysteries and riddles. And here, therefore, many riddles lie. Therefore, understanding is needed by the one encountering such psalms which are so inscribed. And just as it is necessary "to pay attention" to the "reading" of the "God-breathed Scripture," not only of the scriptures but also of "all," so also these owe to speak and to be heard with understanding.

Since, however, the name of understanding is also made clear by proximity and signifies something else in: "but understanding is good to all who practice it." Here the understanding that comes to be and is practiced is moral virtue; for especially this regulates the character of men. He says, therefore, that this psalm ought not to be spoken by voice alone, but also to be understood by the mind and to practice the works appropriate to it, according to the other meaning of understanding, about which also Paul speaks. Writing about ministry and the service toward the saints, he says: "May God grant you understanding in all things" (Eph 1:17); for he does not say understanding as the knowledge of things combined and uncombined, but the practical virtue; for who is so wise as he who has perfected his own character and regulated it? And for himself and for those speaking and those hearing? The one teaching wisely about prudence possesses the virtue of prudence himself, which also those being instructed with him possess; for this reason the right word teaches as a teacher, and especially the one of ethics, so that those hearing might become such as the speaker is. The manner which he intends is like a [light] upon the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spiritual Deer and the Single Desire
english: As the deer longs for the springs of water, so my soul longs for you, O God (Psalm 42:1). This animal is said to be a destroyer of serpents. And when it has killed the serpents, it becomes thirsty from their venom and hastens to find a spring of water, so that it may wash away the thirst and be cleansed; for it is said that as the serpents are torn apart by this animal, they cover the face of the deer with blood and other things, and so it goes away to wash itself, so that the impurity brought upon it from the destruction of the serpents may be washed away.

And something else is said about this animal: that when it grows old and sheds its antlers, it eats serpents and is renewed. The eating of serpents makes it new again. But of what kind of serpents? All the kind of venomous ones, of all the serpents or even of the whole genus. And this too: when it casts off its horns from old age, it dwells in a den until it grows horns again and becomes strong; for one without horns is vulnerable; for they are its weapons and its defenses. Therefore, when they pass through the woods, their horns are seized and thus they are torn away; so a proverb like this appears: 'Woe to deer without horns.' And this proverb alludes to this: woe to the helpless man who does not have the power to help himself.

The other thing of those signified here is shown by the saying: 'In the same way that a deer longs for the springs of water, so my soul longs for you, my God' (Psalm 42:1); he compared the longing toward God to the longing of the deer for the springs; for God is a spring, and His word is a spring: 'You have left the spring of wisdom' (Job 28:12). 'For with you is the spring of life' (Psalm 36:9). And again: 'You have left me, a spring of living water,' God says (Psalm 119:172). And the Holy Spirit is a spring, if indeed all the gifts flow from Him and from Him they have their beginning.

In the same way that the sensible deer longs for the springs of water, so our soul, becoming a deer and a destroyer of harmful things, longs for you, O God. Those who 'are ready to avenge all disobedience' (Hebrews 10:29) are deer, destroying the serpents of injustice. And those having received 'authority to tread...'

The serpents and the scorpions are deer. These deer also pursue the high things. Just as they pursue the springs of waters, so too the high things; for 'mountains are the high things for the deer'. And again the same: 'He who prepares my feet like a deer' (Ps 103:6), so that having been prepared, they pursue the intelligible things.

And since I have often said that the intelligible things seem to be different and different things according to each and every different thought, even though they are the same in substance, the springs of waters which the spiritual deer seeks, and high mountains, are [the same]. Insofar as they are lifted up and given from above, they are high things; but insofar as they water and give birth to rivers in the plains, they are called springs.

Therefore, it must be said and it is morally right: the serpents are pleasures; for pleasure is diverse. And 'being led by various pleasures and desires'. He speaks concerning the faults of women whom the heterodox capture as captives. These therefore diverse deer do not long to find God; they do not seek one single desire. But one desire is the Savior and our Lord himself. Just as he is called wisdom and truth and light and righteousness, so also [he is] desire.

Furthermore, the bride in the Song of Songs, inquiring about the bridegroom, where she can find him, the doorkeepers whom she inquired of, say: 'What is your brother more excellent than your brothers, the beautiful among women?' (Song 1:9). Say [tell me] your own, the other, among the many brothers. And he says: 'My brother is white and ruddy' (Song 4:1), he is not one, he is man and God. Then, passing through his praises, he says at the end: 'His throat is sweet, all desire' (Song 4:16). His word is sweet.

You know that some desirable things are not entirely [so], but they have something unpleasant mixed in; for example, the drinking of sweet wine has something desirable. But when it is taken to excess, it works a drunkenness and is not entirely desire. Again, the sun seen is sweet. But when its flame descends, it has something unpleasant. Therefore, regarding the discourse concerning the marriage, nothing is unpleasant, it is entirely desire, it is entirely love, according to the one saying: 'My love is crucified' (Song 8:6). But the loves of others have something bitter mixed in. Just as 'all desire' is, so also 'all love' is, and for this reason the soul longs.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Thirst for the Face of God
english: My destroying serpent toward God, according to the deer. When you see, therefore, a soul being surrounded by various pleasures and many thoughts, the old age of wickedness, the old man, is cast off, and the new man is clothed in its place, even if you wish to take it as a proverb or as a literal statement. 'Let a female deer and a colt of graces converse with you.'

Let the word be about a woman. The woman is a female deer in relation to the man, if she destroys the pleasures being cast upon her by the hunters. Furthermore, she is also a colt of grace; for she ought to be new according to temperance and grace, to be a colt of the virtues, so that the graces may mount him. For often the virtues themselves are so called according to that which is written: 'a crown of grace,' a crown of virtues. Being light and truth and righteousness according to his thoughts of the contests, she is a multitude of graces. She does not have the multitude in her essence, but in her activities and her desires.

My soul thirsted toward God, the strong and living one (Psalm 63:1). To thirst is often to take hold of love. Thus indeed in another psalm he says: 'O God, my God, toward you I cry out; my soul thirsted for you' (Psalm 63:2); for he who longs for something and asks in order to receive it, thirsts for it. 'Toward God,' therefore, 'the living one.' Just as the divine men, being altogether filled with spirit and always lifted up toward theology, say: 'The Lord lives,' so Elisha said: 'The Lord lives and your soul lives' (2 Kings 4:9). Thus your soul lives just as he whom you have shared in lives. But you, as one sharing in him, live in this way. Regarding something literal, which the Arian ones interpret badly, to see it beautifully: 'Just as the living Father sent me, and I live through the Father' (John 14:19). And they took as a pattern that: as if someone were to say: 'Just as my rational father is, and I am rational, and just as my father is living, I am living.' Since therefore my father is a living thing, and I live through him because he is living.

Son. Just as man is said to be a living being because of the father, since he is a son of a living being. When will I arrive and see the face of God? Men who are still in life thirst for God as the deer [thirsts] for the springs of the waters (Ps 42:1). Yet they do not say that their desire stands at this point; for they are still far from God in some way of relation and disposition, not in place; nor is anything locally far from God, for he 'fills the heaven and the earth' (Jer 23:24). Therefore he who approaches him says: 'Where shall I go from your spirit and from your face, where shall I flee? If I ascend into heaven, you are there; if I descend into Hades, you are there' (Ps 139:7-8).

Thus those in this life having received a vision of the coming age thirst courageously for God, as if they see themselves far off while the evil of the world and the weight of the world and the corruptible are still pressing upon them. And this is so, since in the feasts of the Hebrews it was customary to see three times of the year; for 'three times of the year all your male shall be seen before me' (Ex 23:27), and 'he shall not be seen before me empty' (Ex 23:29). No one shall be seen before him empty.

Since therefore even this one aims for the springs of the waters, he prays to be fulfilled, so that he may arrive and see the face of God not as a ruler but no longer empty. Therefore he asks: [fragmentary]... he reasons: 'When then shall I attain to the perfect good, so that, having seen the face... of the graces being given toward him?' My tears became to me bread day and night (Ps 119:92). He says this because he knew himself still lacking the face of God... [fragmentary]... a lament completing the ascent to virtue, from toil and... [fragmentary]... according to this, indeed, the meaning is said: 'those sowing in tears shall reap in joy' (Ps 126:5). Going...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Tears as Food and Drink
english: They were going and weeping, lifting up their seeds. Coming, they shall arrive in joy, lifting up their gleanings (Ps 126:5). They sow in tears with sweat the seeds of virtue, the seeds of the Spirit, casting them down. When therefore they have harvested, they no longer labor; for they have attained the end of the one striving. When 'going, we were going,' 'we were weeping, lifting up their seeds.' When we were still sowing, having cast down the seed, we were awaiting the perfection of the fruit. When 'we come in joy,' we lift up the gleanings, not yet the seeds. These, therefore, the tears become food for the one desiring to see God and to be gazed upon by Him. Therefore he says: 'My tears became to me bread of days and of night' (Ps 42:3).

I do not weep casually, nor in pleasures, so that at times I might occupy myself with luxury and at times with the weeping of repentance, but also in the dark times; for the dark times are called night. You also have in another psalm a voice saying such a thing: 'You feed us bread of tears and you give me to drink in tears in measure' (Ps 56:8). It is necessary to bring forth the tears of repentance in a measured way, so that they may become bread and drink. And besides, there will be other things that succeed the labor, the offspring produced from the tears.

In that which is said to me every day, 'Where is your God?'; for this reason also I offered so many tears to become food for me, because I heard them saying: 'Where is your God?' (2 Kings 18:33); this also Sennacherib and Rapsakes said: 'Where is the God your God?' And you, Israelite, 'Where is the God your God, that he may save you?' Tears therefore became food for me, but 'in measure,' and I drank them and I ate them; for I knew that the tears and the labor of these things succeed something making joy.

These things I remembered and I poured out upon myself my soul. When in recollection and memory I became of the insults of these ones who were speaking, these my enemies, I did not go out, I did not pour my soul out outside, but upon myself I poured it out. It is such as: 'I was troubled and I did not speak' (Ps 22:14), and what Paul says: 'But we have received the sentence of death within ourselves, so that we may not be trusting in ourselves' (2 Cor 4:8). This also is said concerning Job: previously he says that 'Job did not sin,' and secondly: 'with the lips.'
the intellect
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Thanksgiving as Confession of Wonders
english: Of confession: there is no lamentation when the passage and haste toward the house of God occurs, but rather a rejoicing. For Abraham thus 'rejoiced in order to see my day, and having seen, he rejoiced' (John 8:51). He saw the day of the Lord by arriving into his house, into perfect faith.

The name of confession in the Scriptures signifies two things, so that I may not say a third meaning. The public disclosure regarding sins is called confession, as if one says: 'having been gathered to confess concerning your sins.' This is found in the Epistle of Barnabas, in the epistle according to him: 'having been gathered to confess concerning your sins.' And again: 'confess your sins to one another' (James 5:16). 'I made my sin known to you, and my lawlessness I did not cover; I said, I will disclose my lawlessness to myself before the Lord' (Psalm 32:5). One confesses while wailing and stripping off his former sins.

It also signifies thanksgiving, as if the Savior says: 'I will confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden the divine things from the wise and understanding, and have revealed them to infants' (Matthew 11:25). He does not give thanks for the fact that 'the divine things are hidden from the wise and understanding,' but for the fact that those who are infants have been enabled to see them revealed. These are the ones from the Gentiles who have believed, whereas the wise and the understanding, from whom the divine things are hidden, are those of the circumcision.

[Fragmentary] He cried this out: 'How do you say, We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us? For in vain you were born...' [Fragmentary] 'The wise were shamed and called upon, because they rejected the word of the Lord.' Since they themselves rejected it, the Scripture became in vain to them. For because of the... [Fragmentary] It is said that, when the letters were first being taken, they were found in small scraps; again, they did it with tablets. And since they understood that those written on tablets... [Fragmentary] so that they might have various tools for writing these things. Therefore, 'the wise were shamed and were deceived, because they rejected the word of the Lord; what kind of wisdom is in them?' For how... [Fragmentary] those who reject...

How do you hear the word of the Lord? Thanksgiving, therefore, is manifested through confession. And: 'Let us confess to you, O God; let us confess to you, all peoples. I will recount all your wonders when I take my portion' (Ps 105:45). The one who confesses by recounting the wonders is praising [God], not regarding his own sins.

And again: 'I will confess to you, Lord, with all my heart; I will recount all your wonders; I shall be glad and shall rejoice in you' (Ps 9:1). And a third time this is said: often the harmony and the [thing] joined... 'I will clothe myself in confession and majesty' (Ps 32:1). There is nothing in you... that of virtue which envies your majesty. And again: 'Confession and beauty before him' (Ps 32:1).

Again here the harmony... you do not take confession here as the disclosure of sins... remaining in harmony. The voice of those celebrating this is... having become [it] by voice, but their cry is this: to confess... 'The voice of rejoicing and confession, the tabernacles of the righteous' (Ps 135:4); in those making progress, 'the voice of rejoicing and confession' is, for they were freed from wickedness.

And it is also possible that 'in the tabernacles of the righteous'... when they look up at them and enslave them, when the temples of him... 'Why are you dejected, my soul, and why are you disturbed?' (Ps 42:5)... until someone reaches the house of God. And you, O soul, having remembered... and saying: 'Where is your God?' do not be dejected, do not be disturbed... become. You are able also to receive the angels who are 'celebrating'... 'but you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the festival of myriads of angels' (Heb 12:22). 'Why are you dejected and why are you disturbed?' You have ready the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Light of the Face and the Inner Disturbance
english: Helping. As if even while laboring you say, and while sick: 'Why have you despaired of health? Behold, the physician is present.' Hope in God, because I will confess to him; salvation of my face and my God. God is present; expect from him to be freed from sorrow and trouble. Then he was freed from these, when the sorrows reached an end, when... for he removes the trouble, he removes the sorrow.

'Salvation of my face.' We say regarding 'the eyes of the wise are in his head,' because in the... and the prudent and the imprudent have their faces. 'Salvation...' is said in the scripture regarding the face, which is often said, not regarding... 'May the Lord lift up his face upon you and give you peace' (Num 6:26); for not face... 'May the Lord make his face shine upon you and bless you' (Num 6:25). Here the face that appears... it is also said 'image of the invisible God,' the 'character of his substance' (Col 1:15); salvation and blessing follow, if this face is lifted up and becomes unmixed.

What then is the face? —that which the man took up... a snatching up as if it is the face of God, it is made known... I once also explained into that by a second implication... the Son says the form of the Father, form as his character or form as they construct an idea in the soul. Therefore, salvation is of my face. Having become... it is not that of the body, but regarding that which is said... for it does not say this, that the face of the body without a covering...

Where the face is revealed from ignorance and sin; for 'the wisdom of man brightens his face' (Proverbs 15:30). This bright face does not have a covering of ignorance, nor an overlay of wickedness, but is pure; you are the salvation of the face, O God.

My soul was disturbed toward myself; [this is] the kind of disturbance. And this was also said, when he says, 'I poured out my soul upon myself' (Psalm 62:8) toward the outside; I did not appear to them being disordered. The one being disturbed by these things, his disturbance is turned toward himself.

Therefore I will remember you from the land of Jordan and Hermon (Psalm 133:3). Since my soul is disturbed, even if the disturbance is toward myself, I need a cleansing bath, I have need of baptism. 'I remembered you' therefore 'from the land of Jordan and Hermon'. Hermon is interpreted as 'way of the lamp' or 'offering'. This says that this mountain... acting meteorically, having a divided mind, being illuminated, makes the traveler go straight. And Jordan is interpreted as 'their descent'. It is able to descend, but for their sake it descended, just as an excellent teacher... from a small mountain, the abyss calls to abyss into the voice of your cataracts.

It is, and it is manifest; for 'the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, and let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord' (Psalm 20:6). Even if it is toward us and toward creation, what is being judged together with us. And I say: the Word of God, the God Word, becomes toward each of the prophets; for 'those he called gods, to whom the word of God came' (Psalm 82:6). 'The word of the Lord came to me, saying' (Jeremiah 1:4). If then toward those who are made gods...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Abyss and the Nature of Numbers
english: They do not receive the whole power, the whole participation. Regarding God, the Word was not [separate] from God; the preceding [text says] the Word was God. The Word was not of a different substance from Him. Then, an eternal light from an eternal light.

From this, therefore, the 'small mountain, abyss calls to abyss in the voice of your cataracts'. Listen: in the eighty-tenth Psalm it is said that 'day calls unto day the word, and night declares knowledge to night' (Psalm 19:2). During the day, that which is [shining]. The word of God, when it is luminous and shining and demonstrated, calls out in a manner of harmony, and we understand luminous things from such things; but the deep things [are hidden], for the depth is darkness and night. 'Uncovering the deep out of darkness'.

This darkness is [not the essence], but from that which 'He set as a hidden thing'. Wishing to make clear, we find something else unclear, rather [it is] for the one being instructed, and from that [one] the knowledge, from night indeed, and also here, since the 'judgments' of God are 'abyss' by 'much' in name it is signified. For it is said that 'the abyss is as a garment, his covering' (Psalm 18:4). We know the deep things from the deep. And since they do not all have depth, the very deep things [are known] from those not so deep; the voice of the calling of the abyss to the abyss from those crashing from above it. And it is possible...

But how are the prophets and the apostles flowing? And the apostles. This is the 'abyss calls to abyss' (Ps 42:7). Descending and lying indistinctly, it reaches as far as the voice [is able] to interpret the abyss in the manner of teaching and the [other things]. Then the 'abyss calls to abyss' (Ps 42:7) will clarify it in the manner of harmony.

Now there are 'unutterable words, which it is not permitted for man to speak' (2 Cor 12:4); for he who was caught 'into paradise' (2 Cor 12:4) will speak these. For they are indeed words, and the 'words' are so by homonymy. Then especially are they called 'words'. 'But there is a thought in the soul, sometimes without being true or false, and sometimes the thought which by necessity must have these [two] as something else.'

Psalm to David. Judge me, O God, and judge my cause from a nation of the unrighteous (Ps 35:11). This psalm can be proclaimed from the presence of the Savior. Both the sacred and the profitable lie here. The number six was said to be how it is perfect. But the seven is incorruptible and virgin, barren and without error, as it were; for the seven is not endowed to give birth, nor to be born. A virgin is that which does not give birth, a virgin is incorruptible. Because of this, many times we say [it] occurs not into the six units, but into the nature of the number. We say [it] has come to pass not as a work of the Word needing time, but [as] he simultaneously willed and underwent those things. It is himself: 'all things, whatever you willed, you did' (Ps 115:3). His willing is sufficient for existence.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Numerical Harmony of Genealogies
english: Because of both sequence and harmony, forty-two lies here within a decade. Therefore also in the genealogy there were successions; for it was necessary for the one born from the virgin to be perfect. For every grasping of pleasure comes by the arrival of pleasure.

Just as Saul [the grouping] is from Abraham to David, which in truth are 'fourteen generations' (Matthew 1:17), but from David to the Babylonian exile there are thirteen successions. And since the number fourteen was necessary because of the mystery, he removed the three generations. And again, from the Babylonian exile to Christ, fourteen generations are not found, but twelve in total. And if you even remove Jesus himself, three generations are lacking from the number of the two weeks; for where he removed from the multitude, there he added names to it. Because of the similarity of the weeks, the omission of the three names occurred.

And in the succession he says Joram, Uzziah. And it seems to have the name Uzziah in similarity to that of Jehoiachin; for some consider it to be an evangelical sin, but the imposition of the sin is rather the skill of the wise man, so that he might save the integrity of the numbers. 'Judge me, O God, and plead my cause from an unrighteous nation' (Psalm 7:1). A holy nation he calls, whereas it says, 'Woe to a sinful nation, a people full of iniquities' (Isaiah 5:21). Since therefore he wishes to be judged by this, for they do not have that which I might charge against him; there are no indictments against them. They say, 'This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath'. And what is it to keep the Sabbath? Is it not necessary in the Sabbath not to raise the dead? How does it become a matter of bringing the 'blind from birth' into sight?
By Beelzebul, the ruler of demons
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Light and Truth of the Word
english: the power of God. You are therefore the God... [these things are] manifest. But he, being changeable, needed strengthening... and if he speaks these things concerning the Word of God, he announces them thus: since you are king and... we have explained and also the 'I live because of the Father'; since my Father is living, [it is a] pattern: 'therefore I am rational, because my Father is rational, and therefore I am alive, because my Father is alive'. If then I am my strength, 'why have you rejected me?'; state the reason for the rejection; for I am neither an unholy nation nor an unrighteous and deceitful man. Declare then, 'for what purpose have you rejected me?'; ... I will plunder him, so that becoming a curse, he may provide a blessing... how a sinner was judged.

And for what purpose do I go about shamed, to afflict my enemy? The Jews who believed in him, therefore, knew the reason of how... but so that it might be revealed to the others who surround him in affliction. 'Send out your light and your truth.' 'I have come as light into the world' the man Jesus... to him. But light and truth the Word of God is; for he himself says: 'I am the light of the world', 'I have come as light into the world', and 'was the true light'. 'Send out' therefore 'your light and your truth'.

And may your truth become manifest, then also the reason will be known... and that the man who was benefited by me fights against me unjustly... he wages war against me. Light and truth are not two... light is, when shining, it illuminates the soul and... the lie, or when it has dispelled the shadow of the law. He had the light and the truth; for he was a temple—but...
the mountain of the Lord
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Meaning of Thanksgiving
english: my youth. And this altar, into which someone enters, is an interior one. It is an altar, from which the other of the Seraphim took a coal. And there is an altar in heaven, and the souls of those having been overcome because of the testimony of Jesus (Rev 12:11) are near it. And the word shows that 'those having been overcome because of the testimony of Jesus' are as a priest near the altar. Not everyone is able, but 'the one having been overcome because of the testimony'. Therefore this altar is an interior one.
